sub: Named after “the great news” (an-nabaʾ) in ayah 2; also called ʿAmma
theme: The great news: the Day of Judgement is real. Allah’s everyday signs prove He can bring it about, and on that Day each person meets Hell or Paradise for what he did.
story: Revealed in Makkah in the earliest period. It belongs to a group of surahs, from Al-Qiyāmah to An-Nāziʿāt, that share one theme: the Resurrection and the Hereafter.

The Prophet ﷺ called to three things: Allah alone, his own messengership, and the Resurrection. The people of Makkah mocked the third most of all. They called it impossible and argued about it in their gatherings.

Reportedly, as the Quran came down, Quraysh sat discussing it; some believed and some denied. The surah takes up that very question and answers it: with signs, with the Day, with Hell and Paradise, and a final warning.

sections.title: They dispute the great news of Judgement, warned twice: they will know
sections.meaning: What are the people of Makkah asking each other about? The great news: the Day of Judgement. Some believe in it and some deny it. The answer is a double warning: No! They will soon know. Again, no! They will soon know.
points: What are they asking about? The great news
The news they disagree over
No! They will know. Then again, no! They will know
sections.matters: It sets up the whole surah. The question is the Day of Judgement, and the rest of An-Nabaʾ answers the deniers: with signs, with the scene of that Day, and with its outcome.
sections.story: Reportedly, when the Quran came down, Quraysh would sit and talk about it among themselves. Some believed it and some denied it, above all the news of resurrection, which they thought impossible. These ayat were revealed about that.
explained: ʿAmma means “about what?” It isn’t a request for information; it shows how huge the matter is. They asked half in doubt, half in mockery. An-nabaʾ al-ʿaẓīm, the great news, is the Day of Judgement, or the Quran that announced it.

People split over it: some believed, some denied. Kallā, no! This is not settled by argument. They will know when they face it. The warning is said twice, and the second, after thumma (then), is even heavier.
teaches: Some news is too big to treat as gossip.
The Hereafter can’t be argued away; everyone will face it.
A warning repeated is a warning to take seriously.
sections.hook: An-Nabaʾ opens Juz 30 on page 582. Ayat 4 and 5 are the same words, kallā sayaʿlamūn, with thumma added the second time. The name an-nabaʾ is in ayah 2.

sections.title: Everyday signs of power: earth, mountains, sleep, sky, sun and rain
sections.meaning: Allah points to what they see daily: the earth spread like a bed, mountains as pegs, people in pairs, sleep for rest, night as a cover, day for work, seven strong heavens, a blazing lamp, and rain that grows grain, plants and thick gardens.
points: The earth a bed, the mountains its pegs
Pairs, sleep, night as clothing, day for a living
Seven strong heavens and a blazing lamp
Pouring rain: grain, plants and thick gardens
sections.matters: This is the proof. They said resurrection was impossible, so Allah points to blessings they use every day. The One who made all this with such care can make it again, and such gifts call for thanks, not denial.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the reply to those who thought resurrection impossible.
explained: Alam najʿal: haven’t We made…? Allah asks, and they can only say yes. The earth is a mihād, a bed laid out for homes, farms and roads. Mountains are awtād, pegs holding it steady. People are made in pairs, male and female, for comfort and children.

Sleep is subāt: a cutting off, rest from the day’s work. Night covers everything like clothing, and day is for earning a living. Above are seven strong heavens and a blazing lamp, the sun, giving light and heat. From the clouds pours rain, bringing out grain, plants and gardens thick with trees.
teaches: Every blessing you use daily is a sign pointing to Allah.
Sleep is a gift from Allah, given to rich and poor alike.
The One who made the world can make it again.
Use His blessings to thank Him, not to disobey Him.
sections.hook: It opens with a question, alam najʿal (6), then wa-jaʿalnā (We made) repeats four times: sleep, night, day, lamp (9, 10, 11, 13). Every ayah here rhymes on -ā.

sections.title: The Horn blows on the fixed Day; Hell awaits transgressors for ages
sections.meaning: The Day of Decision has a fixed time. The Horn is blown, people come in crowds, the sky opens into gates, mountains vanish like a mirage. Hell lies in wait for the transgressors, for ages, with only boiling water and pus. It fits what they did: they denied, and everything was recorded.
points: A fixed Day: the Horn, and people come in crowds
The sky opens into gates; mountains become a mirage
Hell lies in wait: the transgressors’ home for ages
No coolness or drink, only boiling water and pus
They denied; all was recorded. “So taste it!”
sections.matters: The deniers asked about the Day; here is what it looks like. It also shows why the punishment is just: they did not expect a reckoning, they rejected the signs, and Allah had written down everything they did.
sections.story: No specific incident. It describes the Day the deniers were arguing about.
explained: Yawm al-faṣl, the Day of Decision, is set: it can’t come earlier or later, and only Allah knows when. The Horn is blown and everyone comes out in afwāj, crowd after crowd. The sky is opened into gates for the angels to come down. The mountains are moved until they look like a mirage, then are gone.

Hell is a mirṣād, lying in wait, the home of aṭ-ṭāghīn, those who crossed every limit. They stay for aḥqāb, age after age. No coolness, no pleasant drink: only ḥamīm, boiling water, and ghassāq, the foul discharge of the people of the Fire. It matches what they did.
teaches: The Day is fixed; denying it can’t delay it.
The punishment fits the crime; Allah wrongs no one.
Every deed, small or big, is written down.
Not expecting a reckoning leads to careless living.
sections.hook: Three inna lines mark its steps: inna yawm al-faṣl (17), inna jahannama (21), innahum kānū (27). Page 582 ends with ayah 30, the section’s last ayah.

sections.title: The mindful win gardens, companions and a full cup: a generous gift
sections.meaning: After Hell comes the reward. The muttaqīn, those mindful of Allah, have a place of success: gardens and grapevines, companions of equal age, a full cup, and no idle talk or lies. It is a reward from their Lord and a generous gift that is more than enough.
points: For the mindful: a place of success
Gardens, grapevines, companions of equal age, a full cup
No idle talk, no lies
A reward from your Lord, a gift that suffices
sections.matters: The surah sets both outcomes side by side: the drink of the Fire, then the full cup of Paradise. And the reward is called both a recompense and a gift: deeds count, but it is still Allah’s generosity.
sections.story: No specific incident. It follows the description of Hell with the reward of the righteous.
explained: Mafāz is success and safety: rescued from the Fire and brought to a place of delight. It holds ḥadāʾiq, gardens of every kind of tree, with grapevines named on their own for their worth. There are companions of the same age, and a kaʾs dihāq, a cup kept full.

No laghw, empty talk, is heard there, and no lies; nobody deceives or denies anyone. All of it is jazāʾ, a reward for their deeds, and also ʿaṭāʾ, a gift, ḥisābā: so generous that one says “enough”. Their deeds matter, but it is still His gift.
teaches: Taqwā leads to the real success.
Paradise is free of idle talk and lies, so leave them now.
Reward for deeds is still a gift from Allah.
sections.hook: It starts page 583 and the second ruku. Jazāʾan returns ten ayat later: jazāʾan wifāqā for Hell (26), jazāʾan min rabbika for Paradise (36).

sections.title: The True Day: return to your Lord now, or wish for dust
sections.meaning: The Lord of the heavens and earth, the Most Merciful: no one dares address Him. Jibrīl and the angels stand in rows; only those He permits speak, and only what is right. This Day is certain, so take a path to your Lord. The punishment is near, and the disbeliever will wish he were dust.
points: Lord of all, the Most Merciful: no one can address Him
The Rūḥ and angels in rows; only the permitted speak
The True Day: whoever wills, take a path to his Lord
A near punishment: “I wish I were dust!”
sections.matters: The surah ends with a choice. After the signs, the Day, Hell and Paradise, it says: whoever wills can return to his Lord now. It closes with the worst regret, so no one reaches that Day unprepared.
sections.story: Ayah 40 is reportedly about two brothers: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, the disbeliever. Other reports name other Makkan leaders. It also applies to every person.
explained: All that reward comes from the Lord of the heavens, the earth and everything between, ar-Raḥmān. Yet no one dares speak to Him without leave. On that Day ar-Rūḥ and the angels stand in rows, and no one speaks unless the Most Merciful allows it, and then only what is right.

That Day is al-ḥaqq, certain to come. So whoever wants can take a path back to his Lord now, through obedience. The punishment is near, as everything coming is near. Each person will see what his hands sent ahead. When the animals are told “Be dust”, the disbeliever cries: “I wish I were dust!”
teaches: On that Day, no one speaks without Allah’s permission.
The door back to Allah is open now.
What is coming is near, so prepare.
Your deeds are waiting for you; send good ahead.
sections.hook: Maʾābā comes back: Hell was the transgressors’ maʾāb (22); now whoever wills takes a maʾāb to his Lord (39). Ar-Raḥmān is named in 37 and 38. The surah ends: yā laytanī kuntu turābā.

groups.text: What are they asking each other about? The great news, the Day of Judgement, which they disagree over.
No! They will come to know. Again, no! They will come to know.
Haven’t We made the earth a bed, the mountains its pegs, and you in pairs?
Sleep for rest, night as a cover, and day for earning a living.
Seven strong heavens above you, and the sun, a blazing lamp.
Rain pours from the clouds, bringing out grain, plants and thick gardens.
The Day of Decision is fixed: the Horn blows, crowds come out, the sky opens, mountains vanish.
Hell lies in wait, the home of the transgressors, where they stay age after age.
No coolness, no drink, only boiling water and pus: a fitting recompense.
They never expected a reckoning and denied Our signs. Everything was recorded. So taste it.
The mindful win: gardens, grapevines, companions of equal age and a full cup.
No idle talk or lies there. A reward from their Lord, a generous gift.
No one addresses the Most Merciful without leave. The Rūḥ and angels stand in rows; only the permitted speak.
That Day is certain, so take a path to your Lord. The disbeliever will wish he were dust.

1.explain: ʿAmma: “about what?” It is not a real query; it stresses how great the matter is. The people of Makkah were talking about it among themselves, half in doubt, half mocking.
1.why: Reportedly, as the Quran came down, Quraysh would sit and discuss it: some believed it, some denied it. When the Prophet ﷺ told them of the resurrection, they asked each other what he had brought. This ayah was revealed.

2.explain: An-nabaʾ al-ʿaẓīm: not just any news, but momentous news. It is either the Day of Judgement or the Quran that announced it.

3.explain: Mukhtalifūn: split over it. Believers accept it; deniers reject it, arguing at length and calling it far-fetched.

4.explain: Kallā: no, never! It cuts off their denial. Sayaʿlamūn: they will soon know, when they face what comes to them for denying it.

5.explain: The same warning again, with thumma (then), making the second heavier than the first. This isn’t settled by debate; the reality will show itself.

6.explain: Alam najʿal: haven’t We made…? A question expecting yes. The earth is a mihād, a bed spread out and ready for homes, farms and roads.

7.explain: Mountains are awtād, pegs, holding the earth steady the way pegs hold a tent, so it doesn’t shake with the people on it.

8.explain: Azwāj: pairs, male and female, so each finds comfort in the other, with love and mercy between them, and children come from them.

9.explain: Subāt: rest, from a root meaning “to cut off”. Sleep cuts off work and worry and restores the body. It is given to rich and poor alike.

10.explain: Night is libās, clothing: its darkness covers everything, so people and creatures rest at the same time.

11.explain: Day is maʿāsh: bright, so people can move about and earn a living. Without it there would be no time to work.

12.explain: Sabʿan shidādā: seven heavens, strong and firmly built, held up by Allah as a roof over the earth, untouched by the passing of time.

13.explain: Sirājan wahhājā: a blazing lamp, the sun. Sirāj points to its light, wahhāj to its heat. Every living thing needs both.

14.explain: Al-muʿṣirāt: the rain-heavy clouds (or, in another view, the winds that squeeze them). Thajjāj: water pouring down in abundance.

15.explain: The rain brings out ḥabb, grain stored as food, and nabāt, plants eaten fresh or grazed by livestock.

16.explain: Jannāt alfāfā: gardens thick and tangled with trees, full of fruits of every kind. After blessings like these, how can they deny the resurrection?

17.explain: Yawm al-faṣl: the Day of Decision, when Allah judges between all creation. It is a mīqāt, a fixed appointment that can’t be moved. Only Allah knows when.

18.explain: Aṣ-ṣūr, the Horn, is blown and everyone comes out of the graves in afwāj: crowds, group after group, each nation with its messenger.

19.explain: The sky is split open and becomes gates and pathways for the angels to come down.

20.explain: The mountains are moved from their places. Sarāb: a mirage. They look like something from afar, but nothing is there, and then they are gone.

21.explain: Mirṣād: a place of ambush. Hell lies in wait, prepared and watching for those headed to it.

22.explain: Aṭ-ṭāghīn: those who crossed all limits and rejected the messengers. Hell is their maʾāb, the place they return to and stay.

23.explain: Aḥqāb: ages, one after another. One ḥuqb is reportedly seventy or eighty years of days each like a thousand years. Whenever one age ends, another begins, without end.

24.explain: No bard, nothing cool (or, in another view, no sleep), and no drink that quenches thirst.

25.explain: Only ḥamīm, boiling water that burns faces and tears the insides, and ghassāq, the stinking pus of the people of the Fire, also described as freezing cold.

26.explain: Jazāʾan wifāqā: a recompense that exactly fits what they did. There is no sin worse than disbelief and no punishment worse than the Fire. Allah wronged no one.

27.explain: Lā yarjūna ḥisābā: they never expected, or feared, a reckoning. Not believing in resurrection, they did nothing for the Hereafter.

28.explain: Kidhdhābā: total, open denial. Clear proofs came to them and they stubbornly rejected them.

29.explain: Everything, small or big, good or bad, is counted and written in a record. No one is punished for what he didn’t do, and nothing he did is lost.

30.explain: It will be said: fa-dhūqū, “So taste!” We will add nothing but more punishment. It is counted the harshest ayah about the people of the Fire.

31.explain: Mafāz: success and rescue. For the muttaqīn, who guarded against Allah’s anger by obeying Him, there is safety from the Fire and a place of delight.

32.explain: Ḥadāʾiq: gardens full of every kind of tree, with rivers running through. Grapevines are named on their own for their worth and abundance.

33.explain: Kawāʿib: in the bloom of youth. Atrāb: all of one age, close companions to one another.

34.explain: Kaʾsan dihāqā: a cup filled to the brim and kept full, a pure drink and a delight for those who drink it.

35.explain: Laghw: useless, empty talk. Kidhdhāb: lies, or people calling each other liars. Unlike drinking in this world, nothing ugly is said there.

36.explain: Jazāʾ: a reward for their deeds. ʿAṭāʾ: a gift of pure generosity. Ḥisābā: more than enough, until one says “enough”; or measured to their deeds.

37.explain: Their Lord is Rabb of the heavens, the earth and all between, ar-Raḥmān, whose mercy covers everything. Yet no one can address Him, or intercede, without His permission.

38.explain: Ar-Rūḥ, most likely Jibrīl (other reports say a vast creation of Allah), and the angels stand in rows. None speak unless ar-Raḥmān permits, and then only ṣawāb: what is right.

39.explain: That is the True Day: it will certainly come. So whoever wills, let him take a maʾāb, a path back to his Lord, through obedience and good deeds.

40.explain: The punishment is near, since whatever is coming is near. Each person sees what his hands sent ahead. When the animals settle their scores and are told “Be dust”, the disbeliever wishes the same.
40.why: Reportedly, “the Day a man sees…” was revealed about Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, and “the disbeliever will say…” about his brother al-Aswad. Other reports name different Makkan men, or take it as general.
